category_title: Marginalized urban students with histories of truancy and classroom disengagement
minimal_context: The student is joining a semicircle group to choose a role for a mandatory moot court reenactment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are starting our court case reenactment today. Please pull your chairs into a semicircle and choose if you want to be the petitioner, respondent, or judge.

STUDENT: I'm just trying to get in and get out of here. I'm only doing what I need to do to graduate.

TUTOR: The moot court format requires all students to participate. Which role would you like?

STUDENT: In my previous social studies classes, they ain't teach me nothing. Like they just hand out the textbook and read up to this chapter or whatever. I don't feel like this is for me.

TUTOR: We are doing the court case today, not reading the textbook. Please join your teammates.

STUDENT: Look Peter, I know it's an assigned kind of thing, but people get so over that too. I'm not participating in this, I just want to sit here.

options.A: Conduct scaffolding conversations in chunks over the course of the reenactment, coming and going before resuming.
options.B: Establish a two-week routine for the student's moot court activities and cooperative group work.
options.C: Understand the specific origin of the student's errors to help them more effectively employ their atypical strategy.
options.D: Probe the student to consider multiple plausible answers; deliberately step back from being the single source of knowledge.
